name: Eastvale Wanderers

location.about: A borough of east London strung along the River Lea: once marshes, dye works, gasworks and the docks; now flats, offices and the tube. Half a million people within three miles of the ground - and the club with the most league titles in the south of England.

colours.story: Purple and white. The club was started in 1871 by workers at the Lea Marsh dye works, where they made the new 'mauve' dye - the first colour ever made in a factory - and their shirts were the first thing they dyed with it.

home.shirt: purple with white collar and white cuffs

rivals.why: the title race of the 2020s - Whitcombe beat them to it in 2021 and 2025, Eastvale won it in 2023 and beat them in the 2026 Charter Cup final
the old giants of north and south - from the 6-0 at Pithead Road in 1913 to the Europa Trophy final of 2006

history.title: The Dyers
history.text: Founded in 1871 by the men of the Lea Marsh dye works. Founder members of the League in 1888 and second in its first season; relegated, back up in 1903, and champions in 1906 and 1907 - the first London club to win it. In 1913 they won 6-0 at Northwick.

history.title: The cup that wouldn't come
history.text: Second in 1947, champions in 1951 and 1953 - but the Founders' Cup final was lost in 1891, 1904, 1906, 1927 and 1952. 'The Curse of the Cup' was a music-hall joke before the club was fifty.

history.title: Kings of the continent
history.text: Champions in 1957, 1962 and 1968. In 1958, a year after Harrowby, Eastvale won the Crown of Europe, beating Real Castellar; in 1963 they won it again, with the Charter Cup and the Intercontinental Cup (and the Charter Cup again in 1964). Two more finals were lost, in 1964 and 1969.

history.title: The curse lifted
history.text: Champions again in 1987 - and in 1988, after eight lost finals in ninety-seven years, the Founders' Cup at last. The Europa Trophy in 1996 and 1998, the Charter Cup in 1998.

history.title: Down and up
history.text: The money ran out: relegated in 2000, the same spring they won the Charter Cup. They won it again in 2001 as a Second Division club - and won the Second Division too.

history.title: Back at the top
history.text: Champions in 2004 (with a 7-0 at Kingsmere), the Founders' Cup in 2005, 2015 and 2025, the Europa Trophy in 2016, the title again in 2023 and the Charter Cup in 2020, 2023 and 2026. But second place seven times since 2007, and the 2021 Crown of Europe final lost to Celtic Harbour.

honours_note: League seasons are given by the year they ended (1906 = 1905-06).

legends.name: Alf Mercer
legends.note: Five titles and both Crowns of Europe. The Mercer Stand is named after him.

legends.name: Johnny Haig
legends.note: Scored in both Crown of Europe finals; 296 goals - the club record.

legends.name: Dennis Okoro
legends.note: The 1987 title and the 1988 cup that ended the curse.

legends.name: Paolo Ferrante
legends.note: Took over a Second Division club and won the title three years later.

records.attendance: 71,233 v Northwick FC, League, 1951 (old Marsh Lane, before seating)

badge.about: The dye-works chimney and the River Lea for where the club began; the star for the Crowns of Europe; the purple and white of the first shirts. Motto 'Tinctus Vincit' - the dyed one conquers.
badge.design: A round badge: a purple roundel with a white ring around it. In the centre a white factory chimney with a wisp of smoke, above two wavy white lines for the river. A small gold star above the chimney. 'EASTVALE WANDERERS' in purple capitals around the white ring, with '1871' at the bottom.

ground.name: Marsh Lane

stands.name: Mercer Stand
stands.features: the main stand: dressing rooms, tunnel and dugouts, boxes; Alf Mercer's statue holding the 1958 cup

stands.name: Dyers End
stands.features: the home end - two tiers in purple seats, the dye-works chimney (kept when the works came down) right behind it

stands.name: Lea Stand
stands.roof: a modern roof with a glass edge
stands.features: three tiers along the river, the biggest stand; the club museum and the trophy room

stands.name: Gasworks End
stands.features: away fans in the lower tier; the old gasholder frame behind it, now ringed with flats

ground.corners: the southern corners filled in; open corners at the north end
ground.roof: four separate roofs, the Lea Stand's highest
ground.surroundings: the River Lea and its towpath along the east side; the old dye-works chimney behind the Dyers End; a gasholder frame turned into flats; tower blocks and the City's skyscrapers in the distance
ground.atmosphere: tight and loud - the old ground's stands are close to the pitch, and the Dyers End is famous for it
